No hosted service, no shared writable store. Each person's design lives at ./.reflow2/graph in their own checkout, git moves it, and genuinely overlapping work is resolved by the three-way merge that already exists — typed per-node and per-property against the common ancestor, with each conflict minted as a Question carrying a deterministic id, and recorded resolutions replayable across near-identical conflicts (rerere). THIS CONFIRMS dec:repo-file-embedded RATHER THAN SUPERSEDING IT. That is the outcome worth noting: this was the first field-sourced re-opening of a settled decision, triggered because dec:repo-file-embedded's own rationale said the concurrency argument was 'hypothetical while there is one writer' and fifteen developers made it concrete. The precondition genuinely changed, the decision was genuinely re-opened, and the original answer survived contact with the new evidence. A re-opening that ends where it started is not wasted — it converts an assumption into a tested position. WHAT WAS REJECTED AND WHY. A HOSTED SERVICE: rejected on cost against confirmed intent, not on taste. It contradicts req:persistence ('the graph lives at ./.reflow2/graph inside the consumer project, so the design travels with the repo') and req:invocation ('the reflow2-mcp binary spoken to over stdio, installed into a consumer project'), both accepted, so choosing it would have required retiring or revising confirmed intent rather than merely adding machinery. It also puts the design on a machine the user does not control, carries permanent operational burden, and breaks the session-transcript identity for everyone but the local user (a local path resolves for one person and silently misses for the rest). A HYBRID — hosted claims and presence over local designs: rejected as the weaker version of the same trade. It keeps req:persistence but strains req:invocation with a second surface to run, and buys live visibility that the claims layer can approximate without a server. WHAT THIS COMMITS TO BUILDING: the scoping primitive (BL-44 cluster claims) so two people do not collide in the first place, and merge-on-pull ergonomics. The counter-argument that belongs in the weighing, so it is not lost: reflow2's loop is built around asking a human and recording an attributable answer — deliberate, sequential, credited — and simultaneous editing may be the wrong shape for that product even where it is technically reachable.
